CHIEF COMPLAINT
Patient presents to discuss smoking cessation.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
44-year-old patient reports being motivated to quit smoking. He has been smoking since high school, initially experimenting with friends at parties. Smoking gradually became more regular, and he now smokes approximately one and a half packs per day, with his first cigarette within an hour of waking. He attempted to quit previously using cold turkey method and was successful for almost a year, but relapsed when work became stressful due to layoffs and increased responsibilities. He is now motivated to quit again, particularly with the upcoming birth of his daughter. He reports starting meditation and recently joining a gym as stress management strategies. He is interested in using a nicotine patch as a smoking cessation aid, based on recommendations from friends who had success with this method. He has chosen next Monday as his quit date, which coincides with his birthday.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
No acute complaints. Patient reports experiencing stress related to work and upcoming fatherhood.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus
2. History of gout
3. Systolic murmur (previously noted, being monitored)

MEDICATIONS
Allopurinol (for gout management)

ALLERGIES
Not documented in this visit.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented in this visit.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Occupation: Currently employed. Patient reports recent workplace stress from layoffs and increased responsibilities. Smoking history: 1.5 packs per day for approximately 26 years, first cigarette within an hour of waking. Does not use other tobacco products. No other drug use mentioned. Upcoming major life event: First child (daughter) expected imminently. Wife present/involved in care. Exercise: Recently joined gym and exercising regularly. Stress management: Recently started meditation practice.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: BP 128/88, HR 68, RR 16, O2 saturation 98% on room air
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm; 2/6 systolic murmur noted (previously documented, unchanged)
Lungs: Clear and equal bilaterally; no expiratory wheezes; no rales or rhonchi
Neck: No lymphadenopathy; no carotid bruits appreciated

RESULTS
None documented at this visit. Hemoglobin A1c ordered for next blood draw in two weeks.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Nicotine dependence: Patient counseled on benefits of smoking cessation for long-term health outcomes, particularly given history of gout and type 2 diabetes. Starting 21 mg nicotine patch on Monday (quit date). Patch location to be rotated daily to avoid skin irritation. Patient to continue exercise routine and meditation for stress management. Follow-up in two weeks to reassess and adjust dosage as needed. Patient given handouts regarding common smoking triggers. Patient to monitor stress levels related to work and upcoming fatherhood.

2. Type 2 diabetes mellitus: Continue current management with diet and exercise. Hemoglobin A1c to be ordered and checked at two-week follow-up visit for monitoring.

3. Gout: Continue allopurinol. Continue to monitor dietary triggers for uric acid elevation.
